transcript.text: Elena, that's an important question and I want to give you a precise answer. The customer agreements require 5 business days' advance notice of a 'material launch delay.' In my reading, the contractual obligation is triggered by an actual or anticipated delay to the release date — not by the mere existence of risk in the execution plan. Committing to the original release date with the substitution, even at zero buffer, does not itself constitute a 'material launch delay' as long as the release date is still the target we're working toward and we have a technically feasible path to meet it. The contracts do not require precautionary notice for risk; they require notice when we know or reasonably expect the release will be delayed beyond the committed date. So if we commit to the substitution today and begin immediately, we are still on track for the original release date, and no notice obligation has yet been triggered. However, I want to be clear about the threshold: if at any point during the 10-business-day replacement window engineering determines that the original release date cannot be met, the 5-business-day notice clock starts at that moment. Given that the replacement takes the full 10 business days with zero buffer, any slip — even a single day — would mean we could not provide 5 business days' advance notice before the delayed release, because we'd have less than 5 business days remaining. That means the practical margin for error is effectively zero not just on the engineering side but on the contractual side as well. My recommendation: proceed with the substitution immediately, but establish a checkpoint — I'd suggest no later than the end of business day 3 of the replacement window — at which engineering confirms whether the original release date is still achievable. If it is not, we trigger customer notice that same day. This gives us the best chance of meeting the release date while preserving our ability to comply with the notice requirement if the timeline slips. I'll also upload my contract analysis to the launch workspace today so it's formally on record for the launch-gate checklist.
